article_content: By Tara Brady Villagers in Russia are mourning the death of a child who was killed when an automatic gate closed, crushing him. The accident happened in the small village of Proskurka, near Novgorod. Four-year-old Vanya Mihanokov was playing near the factory where his mother worked. The automatic gate separated his family's wood processing business from the road. Scroll down for video. The child can be seen on the right-hand side of the picture with a worker playing with a dog. The child is left alone while the worker walks away with the dog towards the road. Vanya Mihanokov walks over to the gate that separates his family's business from the road. Worker Vassily Malenko said, 'Everybody here liked Vanya. He was a sweet little boy with a cheeky smile and polite manners. He brought joy to everyone.' 'The gate was like an adventure for him. He was fascinated by the silent electric mechanism that made it slide open and shut. He would often sit and stare at it for hours.' 'But on this day, he got bored riding his bike around the yard and rushed over to sit on the gate when he saw it moving. His mother, Lioudmila, who was working inside, thought he was safe.' 'A colleague was there, but he didn't see the boy climbing on the gate as it began to move. The boy wanted to get off, but his jacket got caught.' The child's coat gets trapped in the automatic gate, and he begins to struggle. As the gate began to move, the boy struggled to free himself. Vanya Mihanokov was killed when the automatic gate closed, crushing him. 'He was struggling; he couldn't free himself, and then his tiny body was crushed in the closing mechanism.' The other employee didn't see what happened because he was playing with a dog. When he realized what had happened, the boy's mother and staff rushed to the scene, but it was too late. Vanya was declared dead at the scene.

article_content: According to the United Nations, just over 9% of the world's urban population currently resides in megacities. By 2025, the number of megacities, each with a population exceeding 10 million, is projected to increase from 21 to 29. These megacities will then account for 10.3% of the global urban population. Examples of these urban giants include Tokyo, Japan, the most populous with 35.2 million residents – a population larger than that of Algeria, Canada, or Uganda. Shanghai, China, a rapidly expanding economic center, is the world's largest metropolitan area, spanning 2,914 square kilometers. The United Nations notes that megacities can offer wealth, employment, and cultural advantages. Some megacities also demonstrate greater efficiency compared to smaller cities. For example, while New York City is home to 2.7% of the U.S. population, its residents account for only 1% of the nation's CO2 emissions. However, the high population density in megacities can lead to challenges, such as the rapid spread of influenza and psychological issues stemming from poverty and stress. Regardless of opinions, megacities are here to stay and are continuing to grow. Demographia predicts that New Delhi will have 29.49 million inhabitants by 2025, a significant increase from 20.99 million in 2010.

Voorbeelde van hierdie stedelike reuse sluit in Tokio, Japan, die mees bevolkte met 35.2 miljoen inwoners – 'n bevolking groter as dié van Algerië, Kanada of Uganda. article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- Record oil prices, the subprime mortgage crisis, and slumping stock markets are hardly music to investors' ears. In tough economic times like these, investors seek safe, stable investments such as guaranteed government bonds or certificates of deposit (CDs). Yet a growing number are being drawn by the appealing sounds, and potential profits, of a new trend: investment funds specializing in high-end musical instruments. The Stradivarius violin—of which only about 700 are believed to exist—is a premier investment instrument. Talented musicians desire them but often cannot afford them; one fetched $3.5 million at auction. Enter Nigel Brown, winner of The Queen's Award for Enterprise and Chairman of the NW Brown Group, a financial services company, who connects musicians and investors. 'What happens is, a musician comes to see me, having fallen in love with an instrument,' Brown says. 'Then, what I do is to bring together a syndicate of people to buy this instrument so that the musician can then use it...' Eventually, the musician can buy the instrument from the investors, who split the profits if its value increases. That's how violinist Matthew Trusler acquired his $2 million Stradivarius; Brown admired Trusler's playing and funded the instrument himself. 'They are just the most fantastic violins that were ever made,' Trusler says, holding his instrument. 'This one was made in 1711...and it's been around for 300 years; it's a truly wonderful violin.' Not everyone is convinced a Stradivarius is always a great investment—particularly modern instrument makers. 'I think if you can get hold of one of the very best Strads, not just any Strad...I think they probably offer you, as a player, something special,' says violin-maker Andreas Hudelmayer. 'But if you can't have one of the very few best, you are just as well off with a new instrument.' His reasoning: The cost of insuring a Stradivarius for just a couple of years would pay for a new, top-quality violin, Hudelmayer says. Even so, the reality is that old violins are attracting those looking for alternative investments. A new hedge fund called the Fine Violins Fund is dedicated to top-tier instruments. Recent studies indicate exclusive violins have been earning a steady 3.5 percent annually since 1850, which surpasses U.S. Treasury bonds' average yield of 2.19 percent over the same period. Of course, you need to be in it for the long term. 'They've proved to be fantastic investments,' says Simon Morris, director of Beare's—a broker and appraiser of high-end violins, violas, and cellos. 'For many of the musicians that bought, say, in the 1960s, they've been the best pension plan they could've had.' 'Like anything, you have to purchase well and sell well; you can't just buy any old thing.' However, for these investors, the financial return is only part of the investment. 'The fact they make a financial gain is of course gratifying at the end of the day, but it is mostly the support of the musician,' says Brown. 'They like being able to go along to a concert and hear their instrument performed by their artist.'

'Maar as jy nie een van die heel beste kan bekom nie, is jy net so goed af met 'n nuwe instrument.' Onlangse studies dui aan dat eksklusiewe viole sedert 1850 'n bestendige 3.5 persent per jaar verdien, wat die gemiddelde opbrengs van 2.19 persent van Amerikaanse staatseffekte oor dieselfde tydperk oortref. Natuurlik moet jy dit vir die langtermyn doen. 'Hulle het bewys dat hulle fantastiese beleggings is,' sê Simon Morris, direkteur van Beare's—'n makelaar en waardeerder van hoë-gehalte viole, altviole en tjellos. 'Vir baie van die musikante wat byvoorbeeld in die 1960's gekoop het, was dit die beste pensioenplan wat hulle kon gehad het.' 'Soos met alles, moet jy goed koop en goed verkoop; jy kan nie sommer enige iets koop nie.' Vir hierdie beleggers is die finansiële opbrengs egter net 'n deel van die belegging. 'Die feit dat hulle 'n finansiële wins maak, is natuurlik aan die einde van die dag verblydend, maar dit gaan hoofsaaklik oor die ondersteuning van die musikant,' sê Brown. 'Hulle hou daarvan om na 'n konsert te gaan en te hoor hoe hul instrument deur hul kunstenaar bespeel word.'

article_content: By Meghan Keneally Rough state: 'Ice Road Truckers' star Tim Zickuhr was arrested in December; pictured here after being taken to the Las Vegas Police Department. A star of a reality trucking show has been charged with kidnapping a Las Vegas prostitute and threatening to kill her. Tim Zickuhr now faces three felony charges after allegedly threatening and attacking a prostitute who went by the name 'Snow White'. His mugshot, taken in December immediately following the arrest but only released on Tuesday, shows the 40-year-old with bruises or dirt on his face. TMZ reports that he attacked the unidentified prostitute after accusing her of withdrawing too much money from his debit account after giving her his ATM card to pay for her services. Zickuhr joined the History Channel show in its second season, which filmed in 2011, and was sent to drive cargo across some of the most dangerous roads in Bolivia. The show ended after that season. He has since returned to the United States and was in Las Vegas on the night of December 18 when he met with the prostitute. TMZ reports that the pair met that night, and she claims that he gave her his ATM card so she could withdraw an undisclosed amount as payment. Charged: Tim Zickuhr was arrested for kidnapping, extortion, and coercion following a December 19 incident when he allegedly attacked a prostitute in Las Vegas. He later accused her of taking too much from the account, but she agreed to meet him the following day to settle the dispute. As soon as she walked into his apartment on December 19, he allegedly punched her and said he would kill her if she didn't return the money. During the attack, he allegedly used backpack straps to tie her up and then poured cold water over her head from a bucket. She continued to deny taking any extra money, but he gave her a phone and forced her to call someone who would be able to get him the $1,000 he accused her of stealing. She cleverly dialed a police officer friend, and Zickuhr is said to have ripped the phone out of her hand and threatened the officer to meet him. Aggressive: Zickuhr allegedly tied the prostitute up, punched her, and doused her with cold water before threatening her life. Zickuhr allegedly pushed the woman out of a second-floor window as they headed to the meeting, and as soon as they arrived, the officer friend arrested Zickuhr. TMZ claims that Zickuhr 'sang like a canary' and admitted to the threats and violence. He now faces first-degree kidnapping, extortion, and coercion charges and will be back in court in May.

article_content: New York City Police Commissioner William Bratton ordered an extensive review of the NYPD's training procedures following the death of Eric Garner. Garner died after being held in a chokehold while police attempted to arrest him, Bratton announced at a press conference Tuesday. After a two-hour meeting with NYPD Training Commissioner Ben Tucker on Tuesday morning, Bratton ordered a 'top-to-bottom' review of all departmental training, specifically focusing on the use of force, takedown procedures, and authorized levels of force. Bratton stated that he anticipates a re-training of every member of the New York City Police Department in the coming weeks, months, and potentially years. Bratton added that a group of officers will visit the Los Angeles Police Department next week for further training. Bratton led the LAPD from 2002 to 2009, during which time it underwent a 'phenomenal review' of its force policies under federal judicial guidance. Bratton said the LAPD likely possesses the most contemporary policies on use-of-force training, which he intends to leverage. In addition, Bratton mentioned a meeting with the FBI's assistant director Tuesday morning to discuss their monitoring of the incident. He also stated that, based on his experience, he wouldn't be surprised if the U.S. Attorney opened a civil rights violation investigation. A vigil was held for Garner on Tuesday evening, and the NYPD assisted with his funeral on Wednesday morning in Brooklyn. Garner, confronted by police for allegedly selling illegal cigarettes, raised his hands and passively told the officers not to touch him. Seconds later, video footage shows an officer grabbing the 350-pound man in a chokehold and pulling him to the sidewalk, rolling him onto his stomach. 'I can't breathe! I can't breathe!' Garner repeatedly cried, his voice muffled by the pavement. The video shows Garner lying motionless after the incident. Garner, who suffered from asthma, was later declared dead at a nearby hospital, according to CNN affiliate WCBS. Police reported that he suffered a heart attack and died en route to the hospital. New York Mayor Bill de Blasio called the video 'very troubling' and described the incident as 'a terrible tragedy...that no family should have to experience'. Police stated that Garner, 43, a father of six, had a lengthy criminal history, including over 30 arrests, and had been previously arrested for selling untaxed cigarettes in May. Officer Daniel Pantaleo, seen in the video choking Garner, was placed on modified assignment and stripped of his badge and gun while the NYPD investigates the incident, WCBS reported. The NYPD prohibits the chokehold tactic. Two EMTs and two paramedics have been suspended without pay, according to Erika Hellstrom, vice president of development at Richmond University Medical Center. Patrolmen's Benevolent Association President Patrick J. Lynch called Pantaleo's reassignment 'a completely unwarranted, kneejerk reaction for political reasons,' arguing that it 'effectively pre-judges this case and denies the officer the very benefit of a doubt'. On July 19, Garner's friends and family rallied alongside Rev. Al Sharpton in Upper Manhattan, demanding a full investigation into Garner's death, according to WCBS. Garner's wife was scheduled to speak at the rally but was too emotional. New York photographer Joel Graham, who attended the demonstration, shared his photographs with CNN iReport. He said he captured them while walking alongside protesters from New Brighton Church to the store where the chokehold incident occurred. 'This crowd was composed of good, well-meaning people who understood that peace was the only option and were adamant that things remain calm over Eric's death...This was a heartfelt emotional protest because everyone loved Eric,' Graham said. Graham, an area resident, had a casual acquaintance with Garner, explaining that he would occasionally chat with Garner while taking photos near the Staten Island Ferry. 'I had empathy for Eric and how he must have felt trying to catch his breath, and sympathy for the family,' he said. Other related incidents mentioned include: A family of a woman beaten by a California patrol officer plans to sue; New York City to pay a $100,000 settlement to a Brooklyn man beaten by cops; Oklahoma father dies in police encounter after mother slaps daughter.

article_content: Hekmat Kaveh, a 55-year-old millionaire and owner of The Abbey College in Malvern, Worcestershire, which charges £20,000 annually, has been penalized nearly £50,000 for neglecting fire safety protocols, thereby endangering students. He pleaded guilty to 15 violations of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. Kaveh, an Iranian-born property developer residing in a £1.4 million Georgian mansion in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, received a £24,000 fine and must cover £25,000 in court expenses following his court appearance last Wednesday. The Worcester Crown Court was informed that the school, catering to approximately 200 students aged 14 to 20, suffered from faulty smoke detectors and inoperable fire doors, particularly in areas where students slept. Judge Michael Cullum criticized Kaveh for his 'woefully inadequate' fire risk assessment, stressing that Kaveh bore a significant 'moral and legal responsibility' toward the school's staff and pupils. The judge warned that a fire could have had devastating consequences. Following a 2011 inspection, the Hereford and Worcester Fire and Rescue Service initiated the prosecution. Kaveh acknowledged being let down by those tasked with assessing the fire safety. He stated, 'The law clearly states that the employer is responsible, leaving me no choice but to plead guilty. The college now adheres to all regulatory standards. External contractors reassessed the fire safety measures after this issue came to light'. The school, established in 1974 and located on a 70-acre property in Worcestershire, provides GCSE and A-Level courses primarily to international students from affluent backgrounds, with classes averaging just seven students. Deputy Chief Officer Richard Lawrence emphasized after sentencing that lives had been compromised. Lawrence added, 'This was an incredibly serious matter where the safety of those living and sleeping on the premises was jeopardized. Business proprietors have a duty to guarantee the utmost safety from fire hazards for both their employees and the public. This ruling sends a strong signal that we will prosecute in cases of severe negligence, as endangering lives is unacceptable'. The Abbey College's website claims it resides in 'one of the safest and most beautiful areas of central England'. The school is reportedly managed by a limited company. This isn't Kaveh's first legal entanglement. He was arrested in October 2012 for possession of Class A drugs, specifically 38g of opium valued at £100, though charges were later dismissed. Additionally, in August of the previous year, he faced accusations of damaging a neighboring couple's garden. In June of the same year, he was fined £1,000 with £5,000 in costs for improperly using the title 'architect'. The Architects Registration Board took action because he continued to present himself as an architect despite his accreditation expiring in March 2000.

Regter Michael Cullum het Kaveh gekritiseer vir sy 'ontsettend ontoereikende' brandrisiko-assessering en beklemtoon dat Kaveh 'n beduidende 'morele en wetlike verantwoordelikheid' teenoor die skool se personeel en leerlinge dra. Lawrence het bygevoeg: 'Dit was 'n ongelooflike ernstige saak waar die veiligheid van diegene wat op die perseel woon en slaap, in gevaar gestel is. Besigheidseienaars het 'n plig om die uiterste veiligheid teen brandgevare vir beide hul werknemers en die publiek te waarborg. Hierdie uitspraak stuur 'n sterk sein dat ons sal vervolg in gevalle van ernstige nalatigheid, aangesien die in gevaarstelling van lewens onaanvaarbaar is'. Die Abbey College se webwerf beweer dat dit geleë is in 'een van die veiligste en mooiste gebiede van sentraal-Engeland'. Die skool word glo deur 'n beperkte maatskappy bestuur. Dit is nie Kaveh se eerste wetlike verstrengeling nie. Hy is in Oktober 2012 gearresteer vir besit van Klas A-dwelms, spesifiek 38g opium ter waarde van £100, hoewel aanklagte later van die hand gewys is. Daarbenewens het hy in Augustus van die vorige jaar beskuldigings in die gesig gestaar dat hy 'n naburige egpaar se tuin beskadig het. In Junie van dieselfde jaar is hy met £1,000 beboet en £5,000 aan koste vir die onbehoorlike gebruik van die titel 'argitek'. Die Architects Registration Board het opgetree omdat hy homself steeds as 'n argitek voorgedoen het, alhoewel sy akkreditasie in Maart 2000 verstryk het.

article_content: Microsoft plans to showcase its latest Windows software, Windows 10, at an event in January at their Redmond headquarters. However, the actual launch is slated for the fall of 2015, according to Chief Operating Officer Kevin Turner, who spoke with Nikkei. The upcoming operating system is designed to offer a consistent user experience across various devices, including desktops, smartphones, and even the Xbox One. It aims to combine different app stores into a single platform known as the One Store, and bring back the Start Menu, which was absent in Windows 8. Users will have the option to create multiple virtual desktops for better organization. The January event, which will include presentations from Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other executives, will be live-streamed, focusing on the consumer aspects of Windows 10. Microsoft skipped Windows 9 to emphasize the significant changes from previous versions, particularly the poorly received Windows 8. Windows 10 is designed to work on a wide range of devices and is built with a 'mobile first, cloud first' approach. The Start Menu's return is a key feature, blending the traditional list layout with the tile-based interface introduced in Windows 8. The new OS will also adapt to different input methods, such as keyboard and touchscreen, on hybrid devices like the Surface Pro. Microsoft is launching the Windows Insider Program to involve users in the development process, allowing them to test early versions and provide feedback. Industry experts see Windows 10 as a step toward correcting the issues of Windows 8. Stuart Miles from Pocket Lint notes that the new features address many of the annoyances of the previous OS. Geoff Blaber of CCS Insights emphasizes the importance of regaining support from developers and enterprise users. Windows 10 is confirmed to launch later in 2015 and is designed to unify the user experience across various Microsoft devices. Despite the issues of Windows 8 and 8.1, many users are still on Windows 7 or even Windows XP. Windows 10 aims to offer familiarity to Windows 7 users while incorporating some of the benefits of Windows 8, according to Microsoft executive Joe Belfiore. He compares the upgrade to going from a Prius to a Tesla, requiring no significant relearning. The new software allows users to switch between desktop and tablet modes on hybrid devices. Microsoft aims to bridge the gap between PCs and mobile devices, offering a consistent experience across different devices. The unified system will enable developers to create apps more easily for various devices, while consumers can avoid repurchasing apps. Microsoft aims to compete with companies like Apple across multiple platforms, leveraging its position in desktop computing. The company also offers Windows Phone and the Surface tablet to compete with the iPhone, iPad, and Google's Android platform.

Die werklike bekendstelling word egter vir die herfs van 2015 verwag, volgens Kevin Turner, hoofbedryfsbeampte van Microsoft, in 'n gesprek met Nikkei. Die komende bedryfstelsel is ontwerp om 'n eenvormige gebruikerservaring oor verskeie toestelle te bied, insluitend rekenaars, slimfone, en selfs die Xbox One. Dit beoog om verskillende toepassingswinkels te integreer in 'n enkele platform, bekend as die One Store, en om die Start-kieslys terug te bring, wat in Windows 8 weggelaat is. Gebruikers sal die opsie hê om veelvuldige virtuele rekenaars te skep vir beter organisasie. Die Januarie-geleentheid, met aanbiedings deur Microsoft se HUB Satya Nadella en ander bestuurders, sal regstreeks uitgesaai word, met die fokus op die verbruikersgerigte aspekte van Windows 10. Microsoft het Windows 9 oorgeslaan om die beduidende veranderinge sedert vorige weergawes te beklemtoon, veral die swak ontvangs van Windows 8. Windows 10 is ontwerp om op 'n wye verskeidenheid toestelle te funksioneer, en is gebou met 'n 'mobiele eerste, wolk eerste'-benadering. Die terugkeer van die Start-kieslys is 'n sleutelkenmerk, wat die tradisionele lysuitleg kombineer met die teël-gebaseerde koppelvlak wat in Windows 8 bekendgestel is. Die nuwe bedryfstelsel sal ook aanpas by verskillende invoermetodes, soos sleutelbord en raakskerm, op hibriede toestelle soos die Surface Pro. Microsoft loods die Windows Insider-program om gebruikers by die ontwikkelingsproses te betrek, wat hulle in staat stel om vroeë weergawes te toets en terugvoer te verskaf. Bedryfskenners sien Windows 10 as 'n poging om die tekortkominge van Windows 8 aan te spreek. Stuart Miles van Pocket Lint merk op dat die nuwe funksies baie van die irritasies van die vorige bedryfstelsel oplos. Geoff Blaber van CCS Insights beklemtoon die noodsaaklikheid om steun van ontwikkelaars en ondernemingsgebruikers te herwin. Daar word verwag dat Windows 10 later in 2015 bekendgestel sal word, en is ontwerp om 'n eenvormige gebruikerservaring oor verskeie Microsoft-toestelle te bewerkstellig. Ten spyte van die probleme met Windows 8 en 8.1, gebruik baie gebruikers steeds Windows 7 of selfs Windows XP. Windows 10 beoog om 'n bekende omgewing vir Windows 7-gebruikers te skep, terwyl dit sekere voordele van Windows 8 inkorporeer, aldus Microsoft-bestuurder Joe Belfiore. Hy vergelyk die opgradering met die oorskakeling van 'n Prius na 'n Tesla, wat minimale aanpassing vereis. Die nuwe sagteware stel gebruikers in staat om tussen rekenaar- en tabletmodusse op hibriede toestelle te wissel. Microsoft beoog om die kloof tussen rekenaars en mobiele toestelle te oorbrug, en om 'n samehangende ervaring oor verskillende toestelle te verseker. Die verenigde stelsel sal ontwikkelaars bemagtig om makliker toepassings vir verskeie toestelle te ontwikkel, terwyl verbruikers kan vermy om toepassings herhaaldelik aan te koop. Microsoft streef daarna om met maatskappye soos Apple op verskeie platforms mee te ding, deur sy posisie in die rekenaarmark te benut. Die maatskappy bied ook Windows Phone en die Surface-tablet aan in 'n poging om met die iPhone, iPad, en Google se Android-platform te kompeteer.

article_content: A recent survey indicates that the typical person in Great Britain will spend approximately £50,000 on alcohol over their lifetime. This breaks down to around £787 each year, with London residents spending almost an additional £100. However, a significant 1.3 million individuals, considered heavy drinkers, spend nearly triple the average, amounting to about £167,000 on alcoholic beverages throughout their lives. These statistics, gathered for Macmillan Cancer Support, reveal that men tend to spend more on alcohol, averaging £934.44 annually, while women spend approximately £678.60. Regarding preferred drinks, roughly one in three respondents stated that wine is their favorite, followed by beer and then spirits. However, spirits are the top choice among 18-24 year-olds, whereas those over 45 tend to prefer wine. This research, which included 2,000 participants, was conducted to promote the launch of Macmillan's Go Sober for October fundraising initiative. Macmillan encourages people to participate in the Go Sober challenge by abstaining from alcohol during October and seeking sponsorship for their efforts. Martin Lewis from Moneysavingexpert.com commented that the cost extends beyond the price of the drinks themselves; alcohol consumption often leads to impulsive spending. He suggested that even a month of sobriety could result in substantial savings, benefiting both personal finances and individuals affected by cancer. Earlier research from the charity revealed that the average British person spends nearly a year of their life dealing with hangovers, enduring approximately 315 days of headaches and nausea caused by drinking. The survey also highlighted regional differences in hangover frequency, with 22% of northerners reporting more than four hangovers monthly compared to 15% of southerners. Women's hangovers tend to be longer, lasting an average of nine hours, while men's hangovers last around seven hours. The study suggests that hangovers can hinder romantic prospects and career advancement. One in thirteen respondents admitted to missing a first date due to a hangover, and one in ten missed a job interview. Macmillan urges individuals to join the Go Sober challenge, abstaining from alcohol during October and gathering sponsorships. For those with special events in October, a 'Golden Ticket' can be purchased through a donation of £15 or more to a participant's fundraising page, allowing them to consume alcohol on that occasion. Further information and registration can be found at gosober.org.uk. Regrettably, eight percent of those surveyed admitted to missing a wedding due to a hangover, and six percent missed a funeral. Over half cited feeling sick as the most unpleasant aspect of a hangover, while over a quarter found it to be a waste of time. Among those who viewed hangovers as a waste of time, a quarter indicated they would engage in more sexual activity if not hungover. Hangovers also prevented participation in more enriching activities, with 16% stating they would learn a language, 41% indicating they would exercise more, and 13% expressing a desire to learn an instrument. Hannah Redmond, representing Macmillan Cancer Support, emphasized that participation in Go Sober for October, through abstaining from alcohol and securing sponsorships, offers financial savings, health benefits, and the opportunity to raise crucial funds for individuals affected by cancer, ensuring they receive the necessary support.

article_content: Many people have strong preferences for condiments, but few are as devoted as Melissa Ibbitson, a 19-year-old who consumes tomato ketchup at least three times daily. Melissa enjoys ketchup with nearly every meal and once left a restaurant because it didn't carry her beloved condiment. A theology student from Lincoln, Melissa has been a ketchup enthusiast since childhood, but her passion intensified four years ago. She now uses about three bottles of ketchup per week, totaling over 11 stone annually – exceeding her own weight. Melissa recalls, 'I started eating ketchup when I was a kid during trips to McDonalds.' 'I don't remember exactly when it turned into an obsession, but now I can't imagine life without it.' 'My friends often feel embarrassed when I request a dozen ketchup sachets for my meals at the student union, and I always grab extra to take home.' 'I consume so much ketchup that I'm afraid to consider its impact on my health.' Melissa tries to minimize expenses by acquiring ketchup sachets from various locations like the student union, pubs, and fast-food chains. A year's worth of ketchup costs her approximately £300, considering the average bottle price of £1.85. She says, 'Heinz tomato sauce is my preferred brand, but as a student, I sometimes have to compromise.' 'I'd rather use a non-Heinz brand than go without ketchup.' Melissa's dedication is evident through ketchup-themed birthday cakes and Christmas gifts. For example, she owns an 'I love ketchup' tea towel, a personalized ketchup bottle, and a ketchup-bottle-shaped tin. Melissa remembers, 'When I lived at home, my mum would get frustrated because I used the ketchup faster than she could buy it.' 'Since moving out and preparing my own meals, my consumption has increased even more.' 'For breakfast, I eat spaghetti or beans on toast with ketchup. Lunch is a sandwich with ketchup, and I have ketchup with whatever I eat for dinner.' Although Melissa appreciates other condiments, she emphasizes that nothing compares to her love for tomato sauce. She states, 'I enjoy brown sauce and mayonnaise, but I rarely eat them compared to ketchup.' 'My favorite food to eat with ketchup is chips – I can't eat them without it.' 'I've experimented with ketchup on almost everything, and it complements some dishes better than others.' 'Sometimes, I even put it on my roast dinner with gravy, and it tastes great with salad.'

article_content: South Korean news source Yonhap, citing the South Korean Defense Ministry, reported that North Korea fired three short-range guided missiles into the sea off the Korean Peninsula's east coast on Saturday. The ministry indicated they identified two launches earlier in the day, followed by a third in the afternoon, according to Yonhap. These missiles were launched in a northeasterly direction, away from South Korean territory, the ministry stated. South Korea has increased its surveillance of North Korea and is prepared to respond to any potential high-risk developments, the ministry conveyed via Yonhap. The U.S.-based Arms Control Association defines short-range guided missiles as those with a range under 1,000 kilometers (approximately 620 miles). Regional tensions have diminished recently after a tense prior period last month characterized by near-daily war threats from North Korea. U.S. and South Korean authorities had feared that Kim Jong Un's administration was planning a test launch of longer-range ballistic missiles, specifically Musudans. The South Korean government estimates these missiles to have a maximum range of 3,500 kilometers (2,175 miles). Andrew Salmon, a Seoul-based journalist and author, commented that North Korea's reported short-range missile launch on Saturday shouldn't provoke the same level of alarm as a satellite or medium-range Musudan rocket launch. 'It's a short-range tactical weapon. Any other country conducting a similar launch would be considered a routine test and wouldn't cause much concern. The concerns arise primarily because North Korea is the actor,' he explained. Salmon added that the regional situation is currently less strained than the previous month. 'North Korea has substantially reduced its aggression and heated rhetoric since the conclusion of April,' he said. 'I suspect the South Korean government will refrain from strongly condemning this test, as they are very eager to bring North Korea to the negotiation table.' The recent tensions escalated following North Korea's long-range rocket launch in December and its underground nuclear test in February, both of which were widely criticized. Pyongyang's aggressive statements intensified in March when the U.N. Security Council voted to strengthen sanctions against the regime following the nuclear test. Annual U.S.-South Korean military exercises in South Korea also contributed to North Korea's anger, particularly when the U.S. demonstrated its military strength with nuclear-capable B2 stealth bombers. North Korea is seeking recognition as a nuclear-armed state, a demand the United States refuses to consider. The crisis last month resulted in the shutdown of the Kaesong Industrial Complex, which was the last remaining significant symbol of cooperation between the two Koreas.
translated_content: Die Suid-Koreaanse nuusbron Yonhap, met verwysing na die Suid-Koreaanse Ministerie van Verdediging, het berig dat Noord-Korea Saterdag drie kortafstand-geleide missiele in die see aan die ooskus van die Koreaanse Skiereiland afgevuur het. Die ministerie het aangedui dat hulle vroeër die dag twee lanserings geïdentifiseer het, gevolg deur 'n derde in die namiddag, volgens Yonhap. Hierdie missiele is in 'n noordoostelike rigting, weg van Suid-Koreaanse gebied, gelanseer, het die ministerie verklaar. Suid-Korea het sy toesig oor Noord-Korea verskerp en is gereed om op enige potensiële hoërisiko-ontwikkelinge te reageer, het die ministerie via Yonhap oorgedra. Die VSA-gebaseerde Arms Control Association definieer kortafstand-geleide missiele as dié met 'n reikafstand van minder as 1 000 kilometer (ongeveer 620 myl). Streeksspanning het onlangs afgeneem ná 'n gespanne tydperk verlede maand wat gekenmerk is deur byna daaglikse oorlogsbedreigings van Noord-Korea. Amerikaanse en Suid-Koreaanse owerhede het gevrees dat Kim Jong Un se administrasie 'n toetslansering van langer-reeks ballistiese missiele, spesifiek Musudans, beplan. Die Suid-Koreaanse regering skat dat hierdie missiele 'n maksimum reikafstand van 3 500 kilometer (2 175 myl) het. Andrew Salmon, 'n Seoul-gebaseerde joernalis en skrywer, het gesê dat Noord-Korea se gerapporteerde kortafstandmissiellansering Saterdag nie dieselfde vlak van alarm moet uitlok as 'n satelliet- of mediumreeks-Musudan-missiellansering nie. 'Dit is 'n kortafstand-taktiese wapen. Enige ander land wat 'n soortgelyke lansering uitvoer, sal as 'n roetinetoets beskou word en sal nie veel kommer wek nie. Die kommer ontstaan hoofsaaklik omdat Noord-Korea die akteur is,' het hy verduidelik. Salmon het bygevoeg dat die streeksituasie tans minder gespanne is as die vorige maand. 'Noord-Korea het sy aggressie en verhitte retoriek sedert die einde van April aansienlik verminder,' het hy gesê. 'Ek vermoed die Suid-Koreaanse regering sal daarvan weerhou om hierdie toets sterk te veroordeel, aangesien hulle baie gretig is om Noord-Korea na die onderhandelingstafel te bring.' Die onlangse spanning het toegeneem ná Noord-Korea se langafstand-vuurpyl-lansering in Desember en sy ondergrondse kerntoets in Februarie, wat albei wyd gekritiseer is. Pyongyang se aggressiewe uitsprake het in Maart toegeneem toe die VN-Veiligheidsraad gestem het om sanksies teen die regime te verskerp ná die kerntoets. Jaarlikse Amerikaans-Suid-Koreaanse militêre oefeninge in Suid-Korea het ook bygedra tot Noord-Korea se woede, veral toe die VSA sy militêre krag met kernwapen-bekwame B2-sluipbomwerpers gedemonstreer het. Noord-Korea soek erkenning as 'n kernwapenstaat, 'n eis wat die Verenigde State weier om te oorweeg. Die krisis verlede maand het gelei tot die sluiting van die Kaesong-nywerheidskompleks, wat die laaste oorblywende beduidende simbool van samewerking tussen die twee Koreas was.

article_content: Near Cairo, Egypt (CNN) -- Between 15 and 20 people died when two trains collided near Cairo, Egypt, on Saturday night. Officials anticipate the death toll may increase, according to the country's Health Ministry. Approximately 40 to 50 people were injured when a train traveling from Cairo to Asyut collided with another train heading from Giza to Fayyoum, Mohammed Sarhan, Deputy to the Health Minister, told Nile News TV. Sarhan stated that the train bound for Fayyoum was stationary when the collision occurred in the Al-Ayyat district. The collision took place in Kafr Girza, a village within the Al-Ayyat district of October 6 province, Nile News TV reported. Al-Ayyat is located approximately 70 km (40 miles) south of Cairo. The location of the accident presented challenges for emergency responders, Sarhan noted, as the site is adjacent to a water canal. Security personnel used tree trunks and branches to construct a makeshift bridge to access the dead and injured. Nile News TV reported that individuals remained trapped within the wreckage late Saturday. Sarhan added that some of the deceased were found beneath the trains. Government spokesman Ahmed Rady stated that eighty ambulances were dispatched to the scene to transport the injured to nearby hospitals. Rady indicated that the Transportation Ministry has launched an investigation into the cause of the accident. Government investigators are searching for the train's data recorders, according to MENA, the country's official news agency. MENA also reported that Egyptian National Railways has initiated an investigation into the train collision. The governor of October 6 province has ordered compensation for the families of the victims, MENA noted. The Egyptian government has a history of providing compensation to families of train crash victims and those injured in such incidents. Train accidents in Egypt over the past 12 years have resulted in hundreds of fatalities. In August 2006, at least 57 people died and 128 were injured when two passenger trains collided and caught fire in Qalyoubiya Province, located just north of Cairo. In September of the same year, three people died and 24 were injured when a cargo train collided with a passenger train in the same area. More than 370 people died in February 2002 when a fire erupted near the rear of a passenger train en route from Luzzur to Cairo. At least 44 passengers died after jumping from the burning train cars while the train was still in motion.
translated_content: Naby Kaïro, Egipte (CNN) -- Tussen 15 en 20 mense is dood toe twee treine naby Kaïro, Egipte, Saterdagaand gebots het. Amptenare verwag dat die dodetal kan styg, volgens die land se Ministerie van Gesondheid. Ongeveer 40 tot 50 mense is beseer toe 'n trein wat van Kaïro na Asyut gereis het, gebots het met 'n ander trein wat van Giza na Fayyoum op pad was, het Mohammed Sarhan, adjunk van die Minister van Gesondheid, aan Nile News TV gesê. Sarhan het gesê dat die trein wat na Fayyoum op pad was, stilgestaan het toe die botsing in die Al-Ayyat-distrik plaasgevind het. Die botsing het plaasgevind in Kafr Girza, 'n dorpie binne die Al-Ayyat-distrik van die 6 Oktober-provinsie, het Nile News TV berig. Al-Ayyat is ongeveer 70 km (40 myl) suid van Kaïro geleë. Die ligging van die ongeluk het uitdagings vir nooddienspersoneel gebied, het Sarhan opgemerk, aangesien die terrein langs 'n waterkanaal geleë is. Veiligheidspersoneel het boomstompe en takke gebruik om 'n tydelike brug te bou om toegang tot die dooies en beseerdes te kry. Nile News TV het berig dat individue laat Saterdag nog in die wrak vasgekeer was. Sarhan het bygevoeg dat sommige van die oorledenes onder die treine gevind is. Regeringswoordvoerder Ahmed Rady het gesê dat tagtig ambulanse na die toneel gestuur is om die beseerdes na nabygeleë hospitale te vervoer. Rady het aangedui dat die Ministerie van Vervoer 'n ondersoek na die oorsaak van die ongeluk van stapel gestuur het. Regeringsondersoekers soek na die trein se datarekorders, volgens MENA, die land se amptelike nuusagentskap. MENA het ook berig dat Egyptian National Railways 'n ondersoek na die treinbotsing begin het. Die goewerneur van die 6 Oktober-provinsie het vergoeding vir die families van die slagoffers beveel, het MENA opgemerk. Die Egiptiese regering het 'n geskiedenis daarvan om vergoeding aan families van treinstorting-slagoffers en diegene wat in sulke voorvalle beseer is, te gee. Treinongelukke in Egipte oor die afgelope 12 jaar het tot honderde sterftes gelei. In Augustus 2006 is minstens 57 mense dood en 128 beseer toe twee passasierstreine gebots en aan die brand geslaan het in die Qalyoubiya-provinsie, net noord van Kaïro. In September van dieselfde jaar is drie mense dood en 24 beseer toe 'n vragtrein met 'n passasierstrein in dieselfde gebied gebots het. Meer as 370 mense is in Februarie 2002 dood toe 'n brand naby die agterkant van 'n passasierstrein op pad van Luzzur na Kaïro uitgebreek het. Minstens 44 passasiers is dood nadat hulle uit die brandende treine gespring het terwyl die trein nog in beweging was.

article_content: In Wales, an army captain, likely training to join the elite SAS, was discovered dead on a snow-covered mountain during a demanding British Army march. Captain Rob Carnegie is believed to have been participating in a rigorous 17-to-40-mile march in the Brecon Beacons' freezing conditions. This march is part of the selection process for the special forces regiment, during which he collapsed and passed away. The soldier, in his twenties, received immediate first aid from fellow army personnel but could not be revived and was pronounced dead at the scene on Saturday. His grieving family issued a statement honoring the soldier: 'He died while serving as an officer in the British Army, doing what he loved.' Capt Carnegie was stationed at the SAS headquarters in Hereford but hailed from Dublin and served in the Royal Signals. Police are investigating the death of the soldier, whose body was located at Corn Du in the Welsh mountains. A Dyfed Powys Police spokeswoman confirmed the report of a 'sudden death' at 9.42pm on Saturday. 'We are heartbroken by the loss of Rob, a beloved son, brother, and uncle,' his family said in a statement released by the Ministry of Defence. An Army spokesman added, 'It is with deep regret that we confirm the death of Capt Rob Carnegie during an incident in the Brecon Beacons.' 'The soldier's family has been informed and is receiving support. Our thoughts are with them during this incredibly difficult time.' As is standard procedure, the incident is under investigation, and further comment is inappropriate. Each January, soldiers undergo a three-week selection process for the SAS, featuring a challenging 'Test Week.' This involves completing six marches; the initial five are 17 miles, requiring soldiers to march with a 30 kg pack while navigating using a map. At the conclusion of the Battle Fitness Test, they must finish the Long Drag, a 40-mile march completed within 20 hours. Selections occur twice yearly, once in winter and once in summer, to test soldiers under varying temperature conditions. The temperature was below freezing on the 2,907ft Corn Du peak on Saturday night when the soldier collapsed and died. The specific exercise and how far into the march he was when he collapsed remain unknown. His senior officers and fellow soldiers participating in the march are being interviewed by police. Due to the sensitive nature of the SAS, the Army is keeping the investigation confidential. An Army spokesman in Brecon stated, 'An investigation is currently underway.'

As gevolg van die sensitiewe aard van die SAS, hou die Weermag die ondersoek vertroulik. 'n Weermagwoordvoerder in Brecon het gesê: ''n Ondersoek is tans aan die gang.'

article_content: By Toni Jones. An 82-year-old great-grandmother from Cornwall – who may hold a claim to the title of Britain’s oldest punk rocker – is to be the subject of an upcoming documentary film. Sprightly pensioner Viva Hamnell's story of her rise to fame as a vocalist with the legendary Cornish punk band 'The Bricks' in the late 1970s, and her later notoriety during a sensational drug trial, is charted by award-winning director Amanda Bluglass and cameraman Danny Cooke. After the breakdown of her marriage in 1976, the then 45-year-old mother-of-two moved to a secluded farmhouse in the tiny village of St Anne’s Chapel, Gunnislake, Cornwall, to face what she perceived as a bleak and isolated future. The documentary about 82-year-old great-grandmother Viva Hamnell from Cornwall is to be shown on Channel 4. Viva, a mother-of-two, says, 'Punk has a great freedom with no rules'. 'After the marriage split, my life changed, and I sat down on the front step of my new home and literally cried my eyes out,' said Viva. But as the musical and cultural explosion of punk rock gripped the nation over the long, hot summer of '76, Viva soon found herself leading an unlikely double life: as a lollipop lady by day and a backing singer with her 21-year-old son Simon’s punk rockers 'The Bricks' by night. The popular seven-piece band – generally acknowledged as Cornwall’s first punk outfit – soon gained a cult following and garnered favorable comparisons with new wavers 'The Rezillos', as they toured Devon and Cornwall with tracks such as 'High Rise Harry' and 'Dole Queue'. Viva was a backing singer with the 1970s cult new wave band 'The Bricks'. Viva joined her son's band at the age of 45 after the breakdown of her marriage. Viva (wearing the hat) worked as a lollipop lady by day and a backing singer with her 21-year-old son Simon's band by night. 'There was a spirit and energy about punk – it had great freedom with no rules,' explained Viva, who fell foul of the law in February 1979 when an early morning drugs swoop by police discovered cannabis plants growing in her garden, and the bizarre circumstances of her trial made the national press. 'I was in bed on a Saturday morning when the police burst in, and when they asked me what it was, I said: ‘I thought they were tomato plants.’ During the subsequent court case, Mrs. Hamnell was found not guilty after claiming she’d received the plants from a friend and, unaware of their true nature, had intended feeding them to her pet goat. 'It was the worst two days of my life. It was horrendous,' she recalls. 'I didn’t think there was anything sinister,' she explained to the judge at Plymouth Crown Court at the time. 'I just planted them.' The Channel 4 film will touch upon her brush with the law when she was found not guilty of possession of cannabis after claiming it was feed for her goat. While Viva has moved on from the black tights, girl guide outfits, and safety pin earrings of her punk heyday, her current look echoes the creations of Dame Vivienne Westwood. While Viva has moved on from the black tights, girl guide outfits, and safety pin earrings of her punk heyday, her current look echoes the creations of Dame Vivienne Westwood, the pioneering designer who brought punk and new wave fashions into the mainstream. Filmmaker Bluglass, whose recent project 'Ray: A Life Underwater' received 12 film festival plaudits internationally, explained how she was attracted to Viva Hamnell as her latest project. 'A friend told me about Viva, and the minute I met her, I just knew this film had to happen. It’s an incredible story that just had to be told. 'We’ve followed Viva from her farmhouse to Glastonbury, where she has worked for the last thirty years, and reliving her years of leading a punk band to setting up the Elephant Fayre - the forerunner of Cornwall’s renowned Port Eliot Festival.' With the short-edit version of the film soon to be screened on Channel 4, Amanda hopes an internet crowd-funding scheme will allow the purchase of the only known footage of The Bricks performing live and a much longer version of the documentary to be completed. 'This footage, owned by the BBC, is such a find and will transport the viewer back decades. Viva Hamnell keeps a high profile despite her advancing years, with an audience-participation performance where she shares her experiences with small, intimate audiences. 'To me, it’s just my life history, but there’s been so many people along the way, and the punk era, in particular, brought something alive in me. 'I never think I’m 82, as in my head, I’m just Viva, which is Latin for ‘to live’, and that’s what I’ve got to do.' Director Amanda Bluglass says that she knew the story had to be told as soon as she met pensioner Viva. Viva has performed at Glastonbury for thirty years.

Ná die verbrokkeling van haar huwelik in 1976, het die destydse 45-jarige ma van twee na 'n afgesonderde plaashuis in die klein dorpie St Anne’s Chapel, Gunnislake, Cornwall, verhuis om die toekoms wat sy as somber en afgesonderd beskou het, tegemoet te gaan. Die dokumentêr oor die 82-jarige oumagrootjie Viva Hamnell van Cornwall gaan op Channel 4 vertoon word. Viva, 'n ma van twee, sê: 'Punk bied groot vryheid sonder reëls'. 'Ná die huweliksverbrokkeling het my lewe verander, en ek het op die voorstoep van my nuwe huis gaan sit en letterlik my oë uitgehuil,' het Viva gesê. Maar toe die musikale en kulturele ontploffing van punk rock die nasie oor die lang, warm somer van '76 beetgepak het, het Viva haarself gou in 'n onwaarskynlike dubbele lewe bevind: as 'n verkeersbeampte in die dag en 'n agtergrondsangeres saam met haar 21-jarige seun Simon se punk rockers 'The Bricks' in die aand. Die gewilde sewe-stuk orkes – algemeen erken as Cornwall se eerste punkorkes – het gou 'n kultusaanhang verkry en gunstige vergelykings getref met nuwe-golf groepe soos 'The Rezillos', toe hulle Devon en Cornwall getoer het met snitte soos 'High Rise Harry' en 'Dole Queue'. Viva was 'n agtergrondsangeres in die 1970's kultus nuwe-golf band 'The Bricks'. Viva het op 45-jarige ouderdom by haar seun se band aangesluit ná die verbrokkeling van haar huwelik. Viva (met die hoed aan) het in die dag as 'n verkeersbeampte gewerk en in die aand as 'n agtergrondsangeres saam met haar 21-jarige seun Simon se band. 'Daar was 'n gees en energie in punk – dit het groot vryheid sonder reëls gebied,' het Viva verduidelik, wat in Februarie 1979 met die gereg gebots het toe 'n vroeëoggend dwelm klopjag deur die polisie cannabisplante in haar tuin ontdek het, en die bisarre omstandighede van haar verhoor die nasionale pers gehaal het. 'Ek was Saterdagoggend in die bed toe die polisie inbars, en toe hulle my vra wat dit is, het ek gesê: ‘Ek het gedink dis tamatieplante.’ Tydens die daaropvolgende hofsaak is mev. Hamnell onskuldig bevind nadat sy beweer het sy het die plante van 'n vriend ontvang en, onbewus van hul ware aard, van plan was om hulle aan haar troeteldierbok te voer. 'Dit was die ergste twee dae van my lewe. Dit was aaklig,' onthou sy. 'Ek het nie gedink daar is iets sinister nie,' het sy destyds aan die regter by die Plymouth Kroonhof verduidelik. 'Ek het hulle net geplant.' Die Channel 4-film sal haar kennismaking met die gereg aanraak toe sy onskuldig bevind is aan die besit van cannabis nadat sy beweer het dit was voer vir haar bok. Terwyl Viva weg beweeg het van die swart tights, meisiegids-uitrustings en veiligheidspen-oorbelle van haar punk-hoogtyd, weerspieël haar huidige voorkoms die skeppings van Dame Vivienne Westwood. Terwyl Viva weg beweeg het van die swart tights, meisiegids-uitrustings en veiligheidspen-oorbelle van haar punk-hoogtyd, weerspieël haar huidige voorkoms die skeppings van Dame Vivienne Westwood, die baanbreker-ontwerper wat punk- en nuwe-golf-modes in die hoofstroom gebring het. Filmmaker Bluglass, wie se onlangse projek 'Ray: A Life Underwater' 12 filmfees-toekennings internasionaal ontvang het, het verduidelik hoe sy aangetrokke was tot Viva Hamnell as haar jongste projek. '’n Vriend het my van Viva vertel, en die oomblik toe ek haar ontmoet het, het ek net geweet hierdie film moet gebeur. Dit is 'n ongelooflike storie wat net vertel moes word. 'Ons het Viva gevolg van haar plaashuis na Glastonbury, waar sy die afgelope dertig jaar gewerk het, en haar jare herleef van die leiding van 'n punk band tot die stigting van die Elephant Fayre - die voorloper van Cornwall se bekende Port Eliot Fees.' Met die kort weergawe van die film wat binnekort op Channel 4 vertoon gaan word, hoop Amanda dat 'n internet-skarefinansieringskema die aankoop van die enigste bekende beeldmateriaal van The Bricks wat lewendig optree en 'n veel langer weergawe van die dokumentêr moontlik sal maak. 'Hierdie beeldmateriaal, wat deur die BBC besit word, is so 'n vonds en sal die kyker dekades terug vervoer. Viva Hamnell behou 'n hoë profiel ondanks haar gevorderde jare, met 'n gehoor-deelname vertoning waar sy haar ervarings met klein, intieme gehore deel. 'Vir my is dit net my lewensgeskiedenis, maar daar was so baie mense langs die pad, en die punk-era het veral iets in my laat herleef. 'Ek dink nooit ek is 82 nie, want in my kop is ek net Viva, wat Latyn is vir 'om te leef', en dit is wat ek moet doen.' Regisseur Amanda Bluglass sê dat sy geweet het die storie moes vertel word sodra sy die pensioenaris Viva ontmoet het. Viva het al dertig jaar by Glastonbury opgetree.

article_content: Joan Lunden made a courageous decision when she posed for the cover of this week's People magazine. The former 'Good Morning America' host appears with bright eyes and a warm smile, but without her signature golden hair. At 64, Lunden is battling an aggressive form of breast cancer and has shaved her head as she undergoes treatment. Joan Lunden, former 'GMA' host, is battling cancer. While she could have worn a wig for People's photo shoot, the longtime health advocate saw an opportunity to raise awareness. 'I had to make this big decision about whether or not to do the cover with no hair,' Lunden told People. 'It certainly isn't the most comfortable way to go, but I decided I was going to try and help others and show women that this isn't the end of the world. You can go on -- and that was hugely empowering.' Lunden was diagnosed with stage 2 triple-negative breast cancer in June. While sharing the news on 'Good Morning America' that month, she received some valuable advice from breast cancer survivor and 'GMA' co-anchor Robin Roberts. Joan Lunden, former 'GMA' host, discusses her battle with breast cancer. 'Robin told me waiting for your hair to fall out is excruciating. So I didn't want to wait,' Lunden said. 'When it starts to go, it's shocking, embarrassing, and depressing. Pre-empt it. Get it shaved off. I did that. And I thought it was going to be like the biggest deal in the world. And you know what? I felt I didn't have it done to me. I walked in and I said, 'Do this.' After consulting with doctors, Lunden opted for an unconventional treatment plan that involves chemotherapy -- as opposed to the typical mastectomy or lumpectomy -- with the goal of shrinking her tumors so surgery can be minimal. 'You have all these decisions to make, and you have to make them quickly. I had no choice but to go into warrior mode and take this head-on,' Lunden told People. After 12 weeks of chemotherapy, Lunden learned that two tumors had shrunk by nearly 95%. She was able to bypass the second and more difficult phase of chemotherapy, and after a September 23 surgery to remove the remaining mass, she is now focusing on her recovery. 'I was handed an opportunity to learn everything that I can about this and try to help others,' she said to People, 'the opportunity to turn something bad into something good. And that is the most amazing thing.'
translated_content: Joan Lunden het 'n moedige besluit geneem toe sy vir die voorblad van hierdie week se People-tydskrif geposeer het. Die voormalige 'Good Morning America'-aanbieder verskyn met helder oë en 'n warm glimlag, maar sonder haar kenmerkende goue hare. Op 64 is Lunden besig om 'n aggressiewe vorm van borskanker te beveg en het haar kop geskeer terwyl sy behandeling ondergaan. Joan Lunden, voormalige 'GMA'-aanbieder, veg teen kanker. Alhoewel sy 'n pruik vir People se fotosessie kon gedra het, het die jarelange gesondheidsvoorstander 'n geleentheid gesien om bewustheid te verhoog. 'Ek moes hierdie groot besluit neem oor of ek die voorblad met geen hare sou doen of nie,' het Lunden aan People gesê. 'Dit is beslis nie die gemaklikste manier om te gaan nie, maar ek het besluit ek gaan probeer om ander te help en vroue te wys dat dit nie die einde van die wêreld is nie. Jy kan aangaan -- en dit was geweldig bemagtigend.' Lunden is in Junie met stadium 2 drievoudig-negatiewe borskanker gediagnoseer. Terwyl sy die nuus daardie maand op 'Good Morning America' gedeel het, het sy waardevolle advies ontvang van borskanker-oorwinnaar en 'GMA'-mede-anker Robin Roberts. Joan Lunden, voormalige 'GMA'-aanbieder, bespreek haar stryd met borskanker. 'Robin het vir my gesê om te wag vir jou hare om uit te val, is verskriklik. So ek wou nie wag nie,' het Lunden gesê. 'Wanneer dit begin uitval, is dit skokkend, verleentheid en deprimerend. Voorafgaan dit. Laat dit afskeer. Ek het dit gedoen. En ek het gedink dit gaan soos die grootste ding in die wêreld wees. En weet jy wat? Ek het gevoel dit is nie aan my gedoen nie. Ek het ingestap en ek het gesê: 'Doen dit.' Na konsultasie met dokters het Lunden gekies vir 'n onkonvensionele behandelingsplan wat chemoterapie behels -- in teenstelling met die tipiese mastektomie of lumpektomie -- met die doel om haar gewasse te krimp sodat chirurgie minimaal kan wees. 'Jy het al hierdie besluite om te neem, en jy moet dit vinnig neem. Ek het geen ander keuse gehad as om in vegtermodus te gaan en dit reguit aan te pak nie,' het Lunden aan People gesê. Na 12 weke van chemoterapie het Lunden verneem dat twee gewasse met byna 95% gekrimp het. Sy kon die tweede en moeiliker fase van chemoterapie vermy, en na 'n operasie op 23 September om die oorblywende massa te verwyder, fokus sy nou op haar herstel. 'Ek is 'n geleentheid gegee om alles te leer wat ek kan hieroor en probeer om ander te help,' het sy aan People gesê, 'die geleentheid om iets slegs in iets goeds te verander. En dit is die wonderlikste ding.'

article_content: New video has surfaced showing the moment a small plane went down in Hawaii, tragically resulting in the death of Loretta Fuddy, the state's health official known for releasing Barack Obama's birth certificate. The footage, obtained by ABC News, was recorded by a passenger just before the emergency water landing. The cabin quickly filled with water upon impact, but passengers calmly exited the sinking plane. Fuddy, 65, was the only one who died; the other eight, including the pilot, were rescued or swam ashore. The single-engine Cessna Grand Caravan crashed shortly after takeoff from Molokai en route to Oahu, according to Makani Kai Air owner Richard Schuman. Fuddy was seen being helped by her deputy, Keith Yamamoto, but she later died in the water. Coast Guard rescuers arrived to find passengers afloat amidst debris. Passenger C. Phillip Hollstein noted that the plane lost power soon after takeoff, leading to a calm water landing. Hawaii's Governor Neil Abercrombie expressed his respect for Fuddy. Three survivors were hospitalized, while Hollstein and others received care on Molokai. Fuddy and Yamamoto were on the flight following a visit to the Kalaupapa leper colony.

Die beeldmateriaal, verkry deur ABC News, is deur 'n passasier geneem net voor die noodwaterlanding. Die kajuit het vinnig met water gevul ná die impak, maar passasiers het kalm uit die sinkende vliegtuig geklim. Fuddy, 65, was die enigste oorledene; die ander agt, insluitend die vlieënier, is gered of het na die kus geswem. Volgens Richard Schuman, eienaar van Makani Kai Air, het die enkelmotor Cessna Grand Caravan kort na opstyging van Molokai na Oahu neergestort. Daar is gesien hoe Fuddy deur haar adjunk, Keith Yamamoto, gehelp is, maar sy is later in die water oorlede. Reddingswerkers van die kuswag het opgedaag en passasiers tussen die puin sien dryf. Passasier C. Phillip Hollstein het gesê die vliegtuig het kort ná opstyging krag verloor, wat tot 'n kalm waterlanding gelei het. Hawaii se goewerneur, Neil Abercrombie, het sy respek vir Fuddy uitgespreek. Drie oorlewendes is in die hospitaal opgeneem, terwyl Hollstein en ander op Molokai versorg is. Fuddy en Yamamoto was op die vlug ná 'n besoek aan die Kalaupapa-melaatskolonie.

article_content: Following a tragic incident where two skydivers lost their lives due to a mid-air canopy entanglement, the Parachute Center near Lodi, California, remains operational. The accident occurred on Sunday, but by Monday, the facility was open as usual. Bill Dause, the owner of the Parachute Center, acknowledged the somber atmosphere, stating that everyone is deeply saddened by the event. He emphasized that the skydiving community's passion for the sport motivates them to continue, suggesting that the deceased would have wanted the center to stay open. According to Deputy Les Garcia of the San Joaquin County Sheriff's Office, a 911 call prompted their response on Sunday at 12:53 p.m. The Sheriff's Office confirmed the two fatalities and deferred further inquiries to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Ian Gregor, the FAA spokesman, stated that an investigation is underway, with two investigators dispatched to the skydiving center. Gregor mentioned that the investigation might extend over several months. A crucial element of the investigation is acquiring video footage of the incident. The FAA's investigation will encompass various factors, including parachute packing procedures, personnel involved, timing, methods, and the consideration of weather conditions. Gregor noted that they would thoroughly examine how the parachutes were packed, while also acknowledging the possibility that the accident's cause may fall outside of their regulatory purview. Deputy Garcia withheld the identities of the victims, citing the need to confirm identifications and notify their families due to complexities with one victim having multiple names. However, both Parachute Center owner Dause and various media outlets have identified the deceased as Robby Bigley and Barbara Cuddy. These individuals were among eight skydivers from a competition team practicing a 'canopy-relative formation' at 9,000 feet, a maneuver where skydivers create a wedge by stacking their parachutes closely. Dause explained that the last two skydivers attempting to dock experienced canopy malfunctions. One skydiver's parachute became entangled with another, subsequently hitting a third skydiver. While the third skydiver managed to escape, the initial two remained entangled and descended rapidly from 5,000 feet, unable to deploy their reserve parachutes. They landed in a vineyard. Reports indicate that one skydiver died at the scene, and the other succumbed to injuries at a local hospital. Bigley and Cuddy are recognized by the United States Parachute Association as national record holders for formation jumps, with Bigley achieving his record this year and Cuddy in 2007. The team was preparing for an upcoming national competition in October. The United States Parachute Association reported 30 skydiving fatalities in the previous year. Data for the current year is unavailable. The year 1998 saw the highest number of fatalities with 44, while 2007 had the lowest in recent years with 18. Dause mentioned that there had been previous fatal incidents at the Parachute Center but did not provide further details, only stating that the center has been operating for a considerable time.

Die ongeluk het Sondag plaasgevind, maar teen Maandag was die fasiliteit soos gewoonlik oop. Bill Dause, die eienaar van die Valskermsentrum, het die somber atmosfeer erken en gesê dat almal diep bedroef is oor die gebeurtenis. Hy het beklemtoon dat die valskermspringgemeenskap se passie vir die sport hulle motiveer om voort te gaan, en het voorgestel dat die oorledenes sou wou hê dat die sentrum oop bly. Volgens adjunk Les Garcia van die San Joaquin County Sheriff se Kantoor, het 'n 911-oproep hul reaksie op Sondag om 12:53 nm ontlok. Die Sheriff se Kantoor het die twee sterftes bevestig en verdere navrae na die Federale Lugvaartadministrasie (FAA) verwys. Ian Gregor, die FAA-woordvoerder, het gesê dat 'n ondersoek aan die gang is, met twee ondersoekers wat na die valskermspringsentrum gestuur is. Gregor het genoem dat die ondersoek oor etlike maande kan strek. 'n Deurslaggewende element van die ondersoek is die verkryging van videomateriaal van die voorval. Die FAA se ondersoek sal verskeie faktore omvat, insluitend valskermpakprosedures, betrokke personeel, tydsberekening, metodes en die oorweging van weersomstandhede. Gregor het opgemerk dat hulle deeglik sal ondersoek hoe die valskerms gepak is, terwyl hy ook erken dat die oorsaak van die ongeluk buite hul regulatoriese bevoegdheid kan val. Adjunk Garcia het die identiteite van die slagoffers weerhou en die behoefte aangevoer om identifikasies te bevestig en hul families in kennis te stel as gevolg van kompleksiteite met een slagoffer wat verskeie name het. Beide die eienaar van die Valskermsentrum, Dause, en verskeie media-outlets het egter die oorledenes as Robby Bigley en Barbara Cuddy geïdentifiseer. Hierdie individue was onder agt valskermspringers van 'n kompetisiespan wat 'n 'valskerm-relatiewe formasie' op 9 000 voet geoefen het, 'n maneuver waar valskermspringers 'n wig skep deur hul valskerms naby mekaar te stapel. Dause het verduidelik dat die laaste twee valskermspringers wat probeer dok het, valskermwanfunksies ervaar het. Een valskermspringer se valskerm het met 'n ander verstrengel geraak en daarna 'n derde valskermspringer getref. Terwyl die derde valskermspringer daarin geslaag het om te ontsnap, het die aanvanklike twee verstrengel gebly en vinnig van 5 000 voet afgesak, nie in staat om hul reserwevalskerms te ontplooi nie. Hulle het in 'n wingerd geland. Berigte dui daarop dat een valskermspringer op die toneel gesterf het, en die ander het aan beserings in 'n plaaslike hospitaal beswyk. Bigley en Cuddy word deur die Verenigde State Valskerm Assosiasie erken as nasionale rekordhouers vir formasiespronge, met Bigley wat vanjaar sy rekord behaal het en Cuddy in 2007. Die span het voorberei vir 'n komende nasionale kompetisie in Oktober. Die Verenigde State Valskerm Assosiasie het 30 valskermspringsterftes in die vorige jaar aangemeld. Data vir die huidige jaar is nie beskikbaar nie. Die jaar 1998 het die hoogste aantal sterftes met 44 gesien, terwyl 2007 die laagste in die afgelope jare met 18 gehad het. Dause het genoem dat daar vorige noodlottige voorvalle by die Valskermsentrum was, maar het geen verdere besonderhede verskaf nie, en slegs gesê dat die sentrum al lank in werking is.

article_content: Nikki Shelley, a 33-year-old care home worker, transforms herself into eerie characters using face paint. A self-taught artist, Shelley creates monsters, zombies, and ghouls from her home in Rugby, Warwickshire. Her impressive creations have gone viral on Facebook, even catching the eye of special effects experts from the BBC science fiction shows 'Doctor Who' and 'Torchwood'. Shelley's artistic journey began when she painted her children's faces for Halloween, unexpectedly discovering her talent. She stated, 'I didn't think anything would come of it, but the reaction to my work has been incredible. I don't really have a specific idea when I begin painting; I just start and see what emerges.' Married to Craig, 37, Shelley's first subjects were her children Taylor, 13, Leah, 11, and Kaiden, 9. Her portfolio has garnered praise from over 1,000 Facebook users, and her family encouraged her to pursue her passion professionally. Shelley now aspires to turn her hobby into a career. She explained, 'I started painting my kids' faces for Halloween, and then I asked Craig if I could paint him too. But I realized I couldn't paint on them constantly, so I started painting my own face.' Describing her artistic process, Shelley said, 'I began exploring ways to make my work unique. I wanted to stand out and experiment with new techniques. Thankfully, it's been successful.' Shelley finds inspiration in prosthetic designer Neill Gorton, who has invited her to be an instructor at 'The Prosthetics Event' in Birmingham next month. Sharing her home with her husband in a £140,000 three-bedroom semi-detached house, Shelley, whose surname is shared with 'Frankenstein' author Mary Shelley, remarked, 'I never imagined I'd be an educator at a Neill Gorton show.' 'The past 18 months have been amazing. I'm now eager to learn about prosthetics and hope to one day work on TV shows and films.'

article_content: Sean Eldridge, the husband of Facebook co-founder Chris Hughes, launched a campaign for Congress in the past after purchasing a home in a competitive district in upstate New York. Chris Hughes was Mark Zuckerberg's college roommate during the launch of Facebook. Subsequently, Hughes' husband, Sean Eldridge, attempted to leverage connections in upstate New York to pursue a seat in Congress. Speculation about Eldridge's political ambitions arose after he and Hughes spearheaded the marriage equality movement in New York. His campaign was officially announced some time ago through a Twitter ad during an Emmys broadcast. Eldridge previously ran in New York's 19th district. This marked the second time he and his millionaire husband had moved while actively seeking a political career for Eldridge. Criticism regarding his perceived 'carpet-bagger' approach emerged when he and Hughes acquired a $5 million estate in Garrison, New York, only to spend more time in a different district after realizing the difficulty of winning the Democratic nomination there. In 2010, Republicans Nan Hayworth and Chris Gibson were elected to the 18th and 19th Districts, respectively. After one term, Hayworth was defeated by Sean Patrick Maloney, a Democrat with similar political views to Eldridge, making a primary contest less appealing. The New York Times profiled the couple, detailing their purchase of an 80-acre estate in Garrison (in the 18th District, an hour from their SoHo loft) followed by a property in Shokan (in the 19th District, an hour further away). The couple owned a $5 million estate in Garrison, a $4.9 million loft in SoHo, and a $2 million home in Shokan. In a campaign video, Eldridge highlighted his work with local industries through Hudson River Ventures, which he founded to support small businesses. He mentioned being born in Ohio but omitted details about his various moves within New York. 'I love the Hudson Valley; it's where I'm building my home, my family, and my business,' he stated in the video. He also cited a desire to 'reduce the influence of money and special interests in politics' as a motivation for his campaign, notably omitting any mention of his husband. Eldridge became a figure in political circles. Hughes, with a significant net worth, previously ran The New Republic magazine after acquiring it. The couple was known for their philanthropic contributions and their wedding. The formal ceremony took place at their Garrison home, followed by a larger reception at Cipriani restaurant in Manhattan. While the Garrison ceremony included 75 close friends and family, the Cipriani reception hosted 400 guests, including New York Senators and media figures such as Arianna Huffington and Mark Zuckerberg. Although Eldridge's familiarity with the 19th District may have been recent, he and Hughes had been involved in New York state politics for years. The couple initially purchased the $5 million home in Garrison, New York. However, after determining that Eldridge would struggle to win in that district, they bought another house further upstate. Their property in Shokan established them as residents of New York's 19th District. Eldridge announced his candidacy for the Congressional race in that area. He worked for the same-sex marriage advocacy group Freedom to Marry, and the couple raised funds for Governor Andrew Cuomo. Eldridge previously challenged Chris Gibson, the Republican congressman representing the 19th district, who was elected during a surge in Tea Party support. Gibson's spokeswoman, Stephanie Valle, stated that 'this race will test whether Congressional seats can be bought.' She added, 'This comes as no surprise. He purchased a multi-million dollar home in our district, filed to run for Congress, and then resolved his voter registration issues. He's been raising money from wealthy friends while simultaneously promoting an economic plan that amounts to loaning money to his potential constituents.'

article_content: By Francesca Infante PUBLISHED: 05:42 EST, August 15, 2013 | UPDATED: 10:12 EST, August 15, 2013 There was hair-pulling, spitting, and fisticuffs at the school gates – and that was just the parents. Two young mothers have been found guilty of assault after an unseemly brawl outside their children’s school in south London. As Kelly Giles was waiting to pick up her child from Merton Abbey Primary School, she was confronted by Keyleigh Gore, who claimed Giles had called her 'fat' and insulted her daughter. Keyleigh Gore, 25, has been found guilty of assault after confronting a fellow mother who she believed had called her fat. Gore, 25, pushed Miss Giles, who fell back onto a low-level wall, and then started repeatedly punching her. Sasha Fisher, who initially tried to break up the pair, then assaulted Miss Giles by pushing her in the shoulder and hitting her in the face. Miss Giles was left with extensive bruising to her lower back, arms, and above her left eye as a result of the attack. Both Keyleigh Gore and Sasha Fisher were hauled before magistrates following the childish spat outside Merton Abbey Primary School on March 12 of that year. Gore, from Wimbledon, South London, admitted she had pushed Miss Giles in order to 'get her off her' after the two became embroiled in a hair-pulling tussle, she claimed. Sasha Fisher, 21, claimed that she initially tried to break up the fight but later hit Miss Giles in the face in 'self-defence'. Fisher, 21, who lives on the same estate as her accomplice, said she had broken up the two women and that she had later hit Miss Giles in the face with her palm only because she had feared for her safety. After a three-hour trial, both were found guilty of assault by beating after their claims of self-defence were rejected by officials at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court. John Brummell, chairman of the bench, said it was clear that the injuries suffered by Miss Giles were a result of the two beatings dolled out by the other women. Merton Abbey Primary School is where Fisher and Gore attacked Miss Giles in March while the women waited for their children to come out of school. He said: 'The issue in this case is self-defence.' 'We found Miss Gore was the initial aggressor.' 'She pushed Miss Giles onto a low wall and proceeded to punch Miss Giles.' 'Miss Fisher initially intervened but then subsequently assaulted Miss Giles by punching her.' 'The extensive injuries suffered were a result of these two assaults.'

article_content: Cruel parents are under police investigation in Mexico City for allegedly keeping their child locked in a cage. Lisette Guzman Montoya, 28, and Menajem Jurado, 33, were exposed after a local political party's campaign team encountered the situation in the district of Miguel Hidalgo. Politician Evaristo Roberto Candia Ortega, who later tweeted a photo of the child, stated: ‘Our team heard a child crying while waiting at the door.’ Evaristo Roberto Candia Ortega tweeted this shocking photo of the abused boy to aid police in locating him and bringing his 'drug-addicted' parents to justice in Mexico City. ‘Upon investigation, they found a little boy weeping inside a cage, with a dog chained nearby.’ After receiving no response at the door, the campaign team photographed the scene. As they took the photo, someone emerged from the house and acted aggressively. ‘It was apparent to my party colleagues that the individual was either under the influence of drugs or heavily intoxicated,’ said Candia Ortega. 'I find it appalling that anyone would confine their child and subject them to such conditions,' said Evaristo Roberto Candia Ortega. The campaign team left and contacted the police. Upon returning with the police, the residence was empty, and both the child and the dog were missing. The police have not yet located the boy or his parents; therefore, Candia Ortega decided to post the photograph on Twitter. ‘I shared the photograph on Twitter to help locate these individuals,’ he said. ‘I find it appalling that anyone would confine their child and subject them to such conditions.’ According to Candia Ortega, his team learned from neighbors that the couple were drug addicts and often caged the boy due to their unwillingness to care for him. He described their actions as ‘deplorable.’ Local police have stated they are prioritizing the search for the boy and the apprehension of his parents. ‘We are aware of their identities and are dedicating resources to locating them swiftly to ensure the little boy's safety,’ said a police spokesperson. In June, police in the Mexican town of Xalapa discovered a four-year-old boy chained to a balcony as punishment.
